title: Practical Python Essentials: From Syntax to Scripting
summary: Master core Python fundamentals, data manipulation, and file automation through daily hands-on coding exercises.
learning_outcomes: Write readable, efficient Python scripts using variables, conditionals, and loops.
Manipulate structured data using core Python collections like lists and dictionaries.
Build modular code by defining custom functions and handling runtime errors.
Automate practical tasks by reading, modifying, and writing text, CSV, and JSON files.

modules.title: Module 1: Python Fundamentals and Interactive Input
modules.objective: Set up basic scripts and manipulate common data types using inputs and output functions.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.concept: Storing information using strings, integers, floats, and booleans.
lessons.practice: Declare variables representing a user profile (name, age, height, active status) and output a formatted welcome string.

lessons.title: User Input and Type Conversion
lessons.concept: Receiving command-line input from users and casting types for calculations.
lessons.practice: Build a tip calculator script that prompts for total bill amount and split count, returning each person's share.

modules.title: Module 2: Decision Making and Iteration
modules.objective: Control script execution flow using conditional statements and looping mechanisms.

lessons.title: Conditional Execution
lessons.concept: Branching execution paths using if, elif, and else logic operators.
lessons.practice: Write a password validator that checks string length and special character presence, returning feedback.

lessons.title: Loops and Iteration
lessons.concept: Automating repeated tasks using while loops and for loops over ranges.
lessons.practice: Create a loop that prints the multiplication table for a number specified by the user from 1 to 10.

modules.title: Module 3: Structured Data Collections
modules.objective: Store, clean, and retrieve organized data using Python's built-in data structures.

lessons.title: Working with Lists
lessons.concept: Creating, indexing, slicing, and mutating ordered sequences of items.
lessons.practice: Build an interactive task list program allowing users to add, view, and remove tasks.

lessons.title: Key-Value Storage with Dictionaries
lessons.concept: Organizing data into key-value pairs for direct lookups and structural clarity.
lessons.practice: Construct a mini contact management script where users can store and search phone numbers by contact name.

modules.title: Module 4: Modular Code and Robustness
modules.objective: Structure reusable code blocks using functions and protect programs against crashes with error handling.

lessons.title: Defining Functions
lessons.concept: Encapsulating reusable operations using def statements, arguments, and return values.
lessons.practice: Write a unit converter function that converts temperatures between Celsius and Fahrenheit based on a unit flag.

lessons.title: Error and Exception Handling
lessons.concept: Intercepting and handling runtime bugs gracefully using try and except blocks.
lessons.practice: Wrap a user division program in a try/except block to handle ZeroDivisionError and ValueError gracefully.

modules.title: Module 5: File Operations and Data Automation
modules.objective: Interact with external data files to automate real-world reading and writing processes.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Text Files
lessons.concept: Opening, editing, and saving external file data safely using context managers.
lessons.practice: Write a script that reads an existing log file, counts total occurrences of the word 'ERROR', and saves the count to a summary file.

lessons.title: Working with CSV and JSON Data
lessons.concept: Parsing and formatting structured data using standard built-in modules.
lessons.practice: Create an automated script that loads an expense report from a CSV file, filters out expenses below $20, and exports the clean data to JSON.

capstone_project: Develop a Personal Finance Command-Line Application that reads stored financial records from a CSV file, accepts new user transactions, computes categorized monthly spending summaries, and exports a final financial summary report to a JSON file.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and file system familiarity

title: React Core & Interview-Ready Practical Skills
summary: A hands-on, interview-focused React course designed to take beginners from core JSX and component architecture to state management and practical coding challenges.
learning_outcomes: Build modular web applications using functional components and JSX
Manage local and global application state using React Hooks and Context API
Fetch and handle asynchronous data with explicit loading and error states
Explain key React architecture concepts like the Virtual DOM and reconciliation in technical interviews
Solve common React coding interview challenges under timed practical scenarios

modules.title: Module 1: React Foundations & Component Architecture
modules.objective: Build static and dynamic user interfaces using functional components, JSX, and props.

lessons.title: Components & JSX Syntax
lessons.concept: JSX extends JavaScript to describe UI layout, compiling down to standard React element trees.
lessons.practice: Convert a plain HTML user card into a reusable React functional component using JSX.

lessons.title: Props and Data Flow
lessons.concept: Data flows top-down in React via immutable read-only props.
lessons.practice: Pass user profile objects down to child components and render dynamic values with default prop fallbacks.

lessons.title: Rendering Lists and Keys
lessons.concept: React uses unique 'key' props to optimize rendering list items during DOM updates.
lessons.practice: Render an array of interview topics using `.map()` and apply unique keys, refactoring code to remove key-related console warnings.

modules.title: Module 2: State Management & User Events
modules.objective: Implement interactive UI components by handling user events and state changes with useState.

lessons.title: Managing State with useState
lessons.concept: State preserves values across component re-renders, triggering dynamic updates when state setters execute.
lessons.practice: Build an interactive toggle card that exposes hidden interview tips on click.

lessons.title: Lifting State Up
lessons.concept: Share state between sibling components by moving state to their closest common ancestor.
lessons.practice: Create a search filter component that passes query updates up to filter a parent list display.

lessons.title: Controlled Components & Forms
lessons.concept: React state serves as the single source of truth for form inputs.
lessons.practice: Construct a multi-field feedback form with controlled inputs and client-side validation logic.

modules.title: Module 3: Side Effects & Asynchronous Data
modules.objective: Fetch external API data cleanly while managing side effect lifecycles using useEffect.

lessons.title: Understanding useEffect & Dependency Arrays
lessons.concept: Side effects run after rendering; dependency arrays control when effects trigger or re-run.
lessons.practice: Log screen resize events and cleanly remove event listeners using the useEffect cleanup function.

lessons.title: Fetching API Data in React
lessons.concept: Asynchronous operations inside effects populate state once data resolves.
lessons.practice: Fetch a list of tech job postings from a mock API and render them upon component mount.

lessons.title: Handling Loading & Error States
lessons.concept: Production components require distinct state branches for pending, success, and error outcomes.
lessons.practice: Implement explicit loading spinners and fallback UI elements for failed network calls.

modules.title: Module 4: Advanced Patterns & Custom Hooks
modules.objective: Extract re-usable UI logic into custom hooks and manage global application state with Context.

lessons.title: Global State with Context API
lessons.concept: Context avoids prop-drilling by sharing data across deep component hierarchies.
lessons.practice: Build a Light/Dark theme provider and consume it inside nested navigation components.

lessons.title: Building Custom Hooks
lessons.concept: Custom hooks allow extraction and reuse of stateful logic across multiple components.
lessons.practice: Extract API fetching and status state into a reusable `useFetch` custom hook.

lessons.title: Performance Basics: useMemo & useCallback
lessons.concept: Memoization prevents unnecessary expensive recalculations and child component re-renders.
lessons.practice: Optimize a filtered candidate list to prevent re-computation on unrelated state changes.

modules.title: Module 5: Interview Preparation & Practical Coding Challenges
modules.objective: Articulate React principles confidently and solve real-world coding interview tasks.

lessons.title: Virtual DOM & Reconciliation Mechanics
lessons.concept: React compares UI trees via diffing algorithms to execute minimal actual DOM updates.
lessons.practice: Draft a concise 2-minute response explaining the Virtual DOM and answer key theoretical questions.

lessons.title: Coding Challenge: Debounced Live Search
lessons.concept: Debouncing prevents rapid execution of search API requests during rapid text input.
lessons.practice: Implement a real-time user search bar with a 300ms debounce buffer in under 30 minutes.

lessons.title: Debugging & Code Refactoring
lessons.concept: Identifying stale closures, infinite re-render loops, and memory leaks is crucial in senior-led code reviews.
lessons.practice: Identify and fix three deliberate bugs in a broken dashboard component code snippet.

capstone_project: Build an interview-ready Job Application Tracker dashboard that features API integration, search/filtering, persistent state via custom hooks, dynamic modal forms, and dark mode theme switching.
prerequisites: Modern JavaScript (ES6+) concepts such as destructuring, arrow functions, promises, and array methods
